author: A tale from the sewers, written down by a former ratcatcher
pages:
#The Kingdom Below

Under every great city of the north there is another city: a maze of tunnels, cisterns and drains where the light never reaches. Here the skeevers live in their countless thousands, and here, the ratcatchers say, the Skeever King holds court.

#His Majesty

The Skeever King is said to be as large as a dog, with fur gone white from age and eyes like two red coals. He sits on a throne made of stolen spoons and broken cheese crates, and every skeever in the city answers to him.

Some say he can speak. Others say he simply does not need to.

#His Treasury

Everything that is ever lost in a city ends up, eventually, in the Skeever King's hoard. Rings dropped down drains. Coins that rolled under floorboards. The left boot of every pair.

If you have ever wondered where your left boots go, now you know.

#How to Avoid Offending Him

The old ratcatchers have a few rules. Never kill a white skeever. Always leave a crust of bread at the bottom of the cellar stairs on the first night of winter. And never, ever follow the sound of tiny trumpets into the sewers after dark.

I broke the third rule once, as a young man. I will only say that I came out three days later, smelling of cheese, with no left boot.
